Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur

 (State Of M.P. And Others Vs Ramsiya Tiwari)
Dated : 11-05-2023
 Shri Mukund Agrawal - Government Advocate for the appellants/State.
 Shri Ravi Shankar Saini - Advocate for the respondent on caveat.

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This case is listed for admission as well as for consideration of I.A. No.1393/2023, an application for grant of stay, I.A. No.1394/2023, an application for condonation of delay and I.A. No.2011/2023, an application under Order 22 Rule 10(A) CPC regarding intimation of death of the respondent Ramsiya Tiwari.

2. It is submitted by Shri Ravi Shankar Saini, Advocate that respondent Ramsiya Tiwari has expired on 15.11.2020 and although this fact has been mentioned in the caveat, which was filed on 03.01.2023, still the appeal was filed against the dead person.

Although the application under Order 22 Rule 10 (A) CPC was filed on 03.02.2023, thereby once again informing the death of the respondent Ramsiya Tiwari as well as informing the names of legal heirs of Ramsiya Tiwari, still no action has been taken by the appellants, and therefore this appeal should be dismissed as having abated.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
4. On a deeper scrutiny, the picture projects a very shocking and sad state of affair.
The impugned award was passed on 06.11.2019 by Second Additional District Judge, Mauganj, District Rewa in Land Acquisition Case No.01/2015.

entities.text: Second Additional District Judge, Mauganj, District Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present appeal has been filed with a delay of 1113 days.
In an application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act, it is mentioned that the award was passed on 06.11.2019 but the OIC of the case was appointed on 09.10.2020 by Collector, Rewa.

It is beyond understanding that why a new OIC was appointed on 09.10.2020 and what happened to the OIC,
who was looking after the case before the reference Court ?
That is not the end of the matter.

The further submission is that on 11.10.2021, the Law Department granted sanction to file an appeal and it is mentioned that thereafter the OIC of the case obtained relevant document from the trial Court and immediately approached the Advocate General Office for filing this First Appeal.
5.

By making such a submission in paragraph 2 of the application, the OIC of the case has tried to give an impression that immediately after receiving the sanction for filing an appeal, the documents State Of M.P. vs Ramsiya Tiwari on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10587032/
1 were obtained from the trial Court, whereas from the details of the application for certified copy of the impugned award, it is clear that an application for grant of certified copy was filed on 19.01.2023 and it was supplied on 20.01.2023 and the appeal was filed on 25.01.2023.

entities.text: State Of M.P. vs Ramsiya Tiwari
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The application under Section 5 of Limitation Act is completely silent as to what actions were taken by the OIC from 11.10.2021 till 19.01.2023.
But there is another surprising and shocking element in the present case.
Whenever, an order is passed, the party suspecting filing of an appeal has a right to file a caveat.
In the present case the impugned award was passed on 06.11.2019 but the respondent did not file any caveat till 03.01.2023.
It cannot be a co-incidence that an application for obtaining the certified copy of the impugned award was made on 19.01.2023 and the appeal was filed on 25.01.2023.

In all probabilities, the filing of caveat on 03.01.2023, filing an application on 19.01.2023 for grant of certified copy of impugned award and filing of appeal on 25.01.2023 clearly indicates that the respondent was well aware of the movement of file in the office of OIC.

6. The only question for consideration is as to whether the OIC or his/her subordinate officers were deliberately sitting over the matter because of any extraneous consideration or they were negligent in discharge of their duty ?

7. Shri Saini has provided a copy of letter dated 15.09.2022 written by SDO/LAO Tahsil Hanumana,
District Rewa to Executive Engineer, Upper Purva Nahar Sambhag Rewa mentioning therein that the enhanced compensation amount be paid to the legal representatives of the respondent.

Thus,
one thing is clear that in spite of the sanction granted by the State Government to file an appeal, on one hand the OIC was sitting over the matter and on other hand, every attempt was being made to release the amount in favour of the legal representatives of the respondent No.1.
8.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that since the application under Section 5 of Limitation Act has been filed in a most casual manner, accordingly, it is a fit case which should be brought to the knowledge of the Chief Secretary of the State of Madhya Pradesh to look into the affairs of his subordinate, who are either negligent or they are out and out to protect the interest of the respondent at the cost of the interest of State.
State Authorities must realise that State property or public exchequer is not their private property but it is a public money and every resident of State has contributed to it.

9. Accordingly, the Chief Secretary of the State of Madhya Pradesh is directed to conduct a detailed enquiry into the following issues and submit his affidavit:
1.
How the respondent came to know that State is going to file an appeal in the month of January 2023?
2. Why the authorities/OIC in spite of sanction granted on 11.10.2021 did not take any steps to file an appeal ?
3. When sanction to file an appeal was already granted, then why attempts were being made to make payment instead of making an effort to obtain interim order from Appellate Court?

2 4.

sentences.text: On whose table the file was lying and a detailed submissions regarding date wise movement of file from one table to another be pointed out.
5. What departmental action is proposed against OIC and her subordinates ?
6. Whether OIC had any administrative control over her subordinates, if no, then comments about administrative efficiencies of OIC.
7. Live link between respondent and OIC/subordinates.

10. Let an affidavit in support of I.A. No.1394/2023 be filed containing the aforesaid contents within a period of four weeks.
11. List this case on 12th June, 2023 at the top of the list.
(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Shanu State Of M.P. vs Ramsiya Tiwari on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10587032/
